# Aether-X Port Congestion Oracle

> **DATA INTEGRITY NOTICE**: **Brazilian ports feed LIVE operational line-ups.** Santos (BRSSZ), Paranaguá (BRPNG) and Rio de Janeiro (BRRIO) are refreshed from APPA Paranaguá, the Porto de Santos operations panel and Lachmann schedules (`data_source="live:appa+santos+lachmann"`); Rio de Janeiro (BRRIO), Niterói (BRNIT) and Itaguaí (BRITG) come from SILOG PortosRio (`data_source="live:portosrio_silog"`), refreshed periodically in production. The remaining 14 ports serve a **reference seed** (`data_source="static_reference_seed"`). Every API/MCP response includes `data_source` and `as_of`. The 24/48/72h trend is a synthetic projection (`data_source="synthetic_projection"`), not a live forecast. Numbers from the seed are reference baselines, NOT real-time field data.

Congestion signals for 19 ports: **5 Brazilian ports LIVE** (4 validated: Paranaguá, Rio de Janeiro, Itaguaí, Niterói; Santos conditional — queue not publicly exposed), **14 global ports as static reference seed** (not live). Every response carries `data_source` so the consumer knows which is which. REST API, Python SDK and MCP server.

## When should I call Aether-X?

Call Aether-X when a decision depends on **current physical-world congestion at a seaport** — not static port information:

- Before assessing whether a port is currently operationally constrained.
- Before comparing routing/scheduling options involving congested ports (use `get_ports_risk`).
- Before estimating exposure to vessel delay or demurrage (the signal returns USD exposure).
- When current physical port conditions matter more than historical averages.
- When an agent needs a current port-risk signal (`signal.level`) rather than generic port data.

**Tool selection for agents:**
- `get_port_risk(port_id)` — one port: current signal (score, queue, delay, demurrage, confidence, provenance).
- `get_ports_risk([ids])` — compare ports in one call.
- `get_port_trend(port_id)` — 24/48/72h synthetic projection.
- `list_supported_ports()` — discover which ports are covered.

Every response includes a `signal` block with `level`, `live_observation`, `queue_vessels`, `decision_implication`, `as_of` — the machine-readable meaning of the data.

## API

- [OpenAPI 3.0.3 spec](https://aetherx.aether-grid.io/openapi.rapidapi.json): machine-readable contract (RapidAPI-compatible)
- [Example call](https://aetherx.aether-grid.io/v1/port-risk?port_id=BRSSZ): GET /v1/port-risk?port_id=BRSSZ
- [Trend example](https://aetherx.aether-grid.io/v1/port-trend?port_id=BRSSZ): GET /v1/port-trend?port_id=BRSSZ
- [Batch example](https://aetherx.aether-grid.io/v1/ports-risk?port_ids=BRSSZ,CNSHA,NLRTM): GET /v1/ports-risk?port_ids=BRSSZ,CNSHA,NLRTM
- [Public feed (no key)](https://aetherx.aether-grid.io/public/ports): GET /public/ports — all 19 ports (BR live, others reference seed), read-only, for widgets/embeds
- [Interactive docs](https://aether-x-oracle-production.up.railway.app/docs): Swagger UI
- [RapidAPI marketplace](https://rapidapi.com/belegante/api/aether-x-port-congestion-oracle): metered plans (Free / Pro / Ultra / Mega)
- [Terms of Service](https://aether-x-oracle-production.up.railway.app/terms)

## SDKs and integrations

- [Python SDK (PyPI)](https://pypi.org/project/aetherx-oracle/): `pip install aetherx-oracle` — sync + async client
- [MCP server (PyPI)](https://pypi.org/project/aetherx-mcp/): `uvx aetherx-mcp` — gives AI agents the `get_port_risk`, `get_ports_risk` and `get_port_trend` tools
- [Remote MCP endpoint](https://aether-x-oracle-production.up.railway.app/mcp): Streamable HTTP, no install
- [Smithery gateway](https://smithery.ai/servers/belegante/aetherx-mcp): hosted MCP connection
- [Source (GitHub, MIT)](https://github.com/belegante-byte/aetherx-oracle)

- Official MCP Registry: `io.github.belegante-byte/aetherx-mcp` (active) — install via `uvx aetherx-mcp` or remote `https://aether-x-oracle-production.up.railway.app/mcp`.

## Dataset

- [Aether-X Global Port Congestion Snapshot (Hugging Face)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Aether-x/aetherx-port-congestion-metrics): frozen 16-port reference CSV, CC BY 4.0
- [Aether-X Port Congestion Dashboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/Aether-x/aetherx-port-congestion-dashboard): static reference dashboard, no key
- [DEV article](https://dev.to/giovanni_belegante_2b04c5/predicting-global-port-congestion-in-real-time-with-python-duckdb-and-mcp-1ahm): describes the live design; live line-ups for BR ports are now connected

## Writing

- [Predicting Global Port Congestion in Real-Time with Python, DuckDB and MCP](https://dev.to/giovanni_belegante_2b04c5/predicting-global-port-congestion-in-real-time-with-python-duckdb-and-mcp-1ahm): DEV Community (the live line-ups are now connected for BR ports)

## Supported ports

AEDXB, BRITG, BRNIT, BRPNG, BRRIO, BRSSZ, CNNGB, CNSHA, CNTAO, DEHAM, GBLGP, KRPUS, MPTNG, MXZLO, NLRTM, SGSIN, USLAX, USNYC, ZACPT

Unknown ports fall back to a global statistical estimate (`country="Global"`).

## Notes

- Signals are provided "AS IS" and do not constitute investment advice.
- Metered access is available through the RapidAPI gateway (X-RapidAPI-Key).
